newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes cool, some vols decline.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Indexes cool, some vols decline.

text.p: U.S. stock index options trading was on the quiet side Thursday as investors watched to see how the market fared after two consecutive record high closes, traders said.
Traders said one institution was a heavy seller of August 950 options on S&P 500 futures calls and another was selling some S&P 500 puts, both pushing volatilities down.

"They're crushing volatility," said one S&P 500 futures-options trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. He pegged volatility in the August series at around 19.7, down about two points over the last two days.
The trader said the institution had begun selling the August calls at the CME Wednesday.
Index options traders said overall activity was light.
"There's really not much action going on today," one said. "A lot of people feel that the (market) top is in and that we had to test the top again."
By about 1240 CDT/1740 GMT, the blue chip Dow industrial average .DJI was down 42 points at 8,046 after tacking on about 180 points in the last two sessions. The average hit a session low of 7,993.
Among other indexes, the S&P 500 .SPX lost 3.72 to 932.84 and September S&P 500 futures were down 3.35 at 937.90. The S&P 100 index .OEX eased nearly five points to 911.42.
The futures-options trader said the firm selling the calls had sold about 1,000 contracts through midday Thursday.
Active SPX puts included the August 900s with volume of more than 3,000 contracts, the August 930s with 2,630 and the August 915s with 2,095.
Few SPX calls were busy, with action led by the August 930s, which traded nearly 1,300 contracts.
The trader at the CME said he expected one more burst to the upside before an extended correction sets in over the near term.
"I do not see a rally in this market being strong at least maybe until next week some time," he added.

Jerry Hegarty, an options analyst at Thomson Financial Services, said in the first three days of the August expiration cycle, which began Monday, 123,000 more OEX puts had traded than calls, a potentially bullish trend.
"If that pattern remains intact, you can go to the bank on the market trading much higher through the August 15 expiration," he said.
Chris Cadbury, who publishes a daily market letter, advised traders to go short "once the downward momentum of the market begins."
